questions.question: What is the most powerful weapon that enables the Parliament to ensure executive accountability?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **The no-confidence motion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **No-confidence motion** is a statement or vote about whether a person in a position of responsibility is still deemed fit to hold that position.
 
• It is the most powerful weapon available to the Parliament to ensure **executive accountability**.
 
• If the motion is passed, it implies that the current government no longer has the support of the majority of the members of the Parliament.
 
• This can lead to the resignation of the Prime Minister and the entire Council of Ministers.
 
• The motion is typically moved by the opposition to challenge the government’s legitimacy and performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Term
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **No-confidence motion**
 A motion moved by a member of the Parliament expressing lack of trust in the government’s ability to govern.
 
 

 **Executive Accountability**
 The responsibility of the executive branch of government to the legislature and, through it, to the public.
 
 

 **Parliament**
 The supreme legislative body of a country, consisting of elected representatives.
 
 

 **Opposition**
 The political parties or groups that are not in power and challenge the government’s policies and actions.
 
 

 **Prime Minister**
 The head of the government in parliamentary systems, responsible for running the executive branch.

questions.question: Where is the Mahabodhi temple situated?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is__** Bodh Gaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The** Mahabodhi Temple Complex, Bodh Gaya** lies 115 km south of the state capital of Bihar, Patna and 16 km from the district headquarters at Gaya, in Eastern India.
 
• It is **one of the four holy sites related to the life of the Lord Buddha**, and particularly to the attainment of Enlightenment.
 
• The property encompasses the greatest remains of the 5th-6th century A.D in the Indian sub-continent belonging to this period of antiquity.
 
• The property has a total area of 4.8600 ha.
 
• The Mahabodhi Temple Complex is the first temple **built by Emperor Asoka in the 3rd century B.C**., and the present temple dates from the 5th–6th centuries.
 
• It is one of the earliest Buddhist temples built entirely in brick, still standing, from the late Gupta period and it is considered to have had significant influence in the development of brick architecture over the centuries.

questions.question: In which year was the Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment (TRYSEM) scheme launched by Government of India?

__
 
• **TRYSEM** stands for **Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment**.
 
• The scheme was launched in the year **1979** by the Government of India.
 
• The main objective was to provide technical and entrepreneurial skills to rural youth.
 
• It aimed to improve the employability of rural youth and reduce rural unemployment.
 
• TRYSEM was later merged with other schemes to form the **Swarna Jayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)** in 1999.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Program
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **TRYSEM**
 A scheme aimed at providing technical and entrepreneurial training to rural youth to improve their employability.
 
 

 **SGSY**
 A scheme that merged TRYSEM and other rural development programs to create a holistic approach to rural employment and poverty alleviation.
 
 

 **NRLM**
 The National Rural Livelihoods Mission, which aims to reduce poverty by enabling the poor households to access gainful self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities.
 
 

 **PMKVY**
 Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, a scheme to provide skill training to youth across the country, including rural areas.

questions.question: What is the usual term used to describe the climate of India?

__
 
• **India's climate** is predominantly influenced by the monsoon winds.
 
• The country experiences **hot summers, wet monsoon seasons**, and mild winters.
 
• The monsoon season accounts for the majority of India's annual **rainfall**.
 
• This climate type is characterized by **seasonal reversal** in wind direction.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Polar climate
 This climate is characterized by extremely cold temperatures and is found in regions like Antarctica and the Arctic.
 
 

 Tropical monsoon
 This climate features high temperatures and significant seasonal rainfall, influenced by monsoon winds.
 
 

 Desert climate
 Marked by very low rainfall and extreme temperatures, typical of deserts like the Sahara.
 
 

 Arid climate
 This type of climate is dry, with very little precipitation, and can be found in areas like the Middle East.

__

• The Census of India 2011 provides data on sex ratios for various states and union territories.

questions.question: Who among the following established a unit of horsepower that is equal to one horse doing 33,000 foot - pounds of work in one minute?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **James Watt**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Watt** was a Scottish inventor and mechanical engineer.
 
• He is best known for his work on the **steam engine**, which played a crucial role in the Industrial Revolution.
 
• Watt introduced the concept of **horsepower** to quantify the power of engines.
 
• One unit of horsepower is defined as one horse doing **33,000 foot-pounds of work** in one minute.
 
• His improvements to the steam engine significantly increased its efficiency and utility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Term
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Horsepower**
 A unit of power that measures the rate at which work is done. Defined as 33,000 foot-pounds per minute.
 
 

 **Steam Engine**
 A heat engine that performs mechanical work using steam as its working fluid. Improved by James Watt.
 
 

 **Industrial Revolution**
 A period of major industrialization that took place during the late 1700s and early 1800s.
 
 

 **Foot-Pound**
 A unit of work in the English system, representing the work done by a force of one pound acting through a distance of one foot.
 
 

 **Efficiency**
 The ratio of the useful work performed by a machine or in a process to the total energy expended.

questions.question: In which year was the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **1976**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act** is one of the most significant amendments to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It was passed in the year **1976** during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• The amendment is also known as the **"Mini-Constitution"** due to the extensive changes it introduced.
 
• Key changes included the addition of the words **"Socialist," "Secular,"** and **"Integrity"** to the Preamble.
 
• It also curtailed the power of the judiciary and increased the powers of the Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Area of Change
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Preamble**
 Added the words **"Socialist," "Secular,"** and **"Integrity"**.
 
 

 **Directive Principles**
 Made them more comprehensive and emphasized their importance.
 
 

 **Judiciary**
 Reduced the power of the judiciary in favor of the Parliament.
 
 

 **Fundamental Duties**
 Introduced a list of **Fundamental Duties** for citizens.
 
 

 **Emergency Provisions**
 Made significant changes to the **Emergency Provisions** in the Constitution.

questions.question: Insufficient levels of parathyroid hormone and low amount of calcium in the blood causes which of the following conditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Hypocalcemia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hypocalcemia** is a condition characterized by low levels of calcium in the blood.
 
• It can be caused by insufficient levels of **parathyroid hormone** (PTH), which regulates calcium levels in the blood.
 
• Common symptoms include muscle cramps, numbness, and tingling in the fingers.
 
• Severe hypocalcemia can lead to cardiac issues and neurological problems.
 
• Treatment often involves calcium and vitamin D supplements to restore normal calcium levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Function
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Parathyroid Hormone (PTH)**
 **Regulates calcium** levels in the blood by increasing calcium absorption from the diet, releasing calcium from bones, and conserving calcium in the kidneys.
 
 

 **Calcium**
 An essential mineral for **bone health**, muscle function, nerve signaling, and blood clotting.
 
 

 **Vitamin D**
 Helps in the **absorption of calcium** from the digestive tract and maintains adequate serum calcium and phosphate levels.
 
 

 **Hypocalcemia Symptoms**
 Include **muscle cramps**, spasms, numbness, and tingling in the extremities.
 
 

 **Treatment**
 Typically involves **calcium supplements** and sometimes vitamin D supplements to restore normal calcium levels.

questions.question: What is a dimension related to the sustainability of microfinance institutions in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Dependency on donor funding**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dependency on donor funding** impacts the long-term sustainability of microfinance institutions as it makes them reliant on external sources.
 
• Microfinance institutions need to develop independent revenue models to be self-sustainable.
 
• Excessive reliance on donor funds can lead to financial instability if the funding stops.
 
• Developing a diverse funding base, including client savings, can enhance sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Microfinance
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Definition
 **Microfinance** refers to financial services provided to low-income individuals or groups who typically lack access to traditional banking.
 
 

 Services
 It includes **microloans**, savings, insurance, and other financial products.
 
 

 Objective
 The primary goal is to promote **financial inclusion** and empower marginalized communities.
 
 

 Key Players
 These include **NGOs**, cooperatives, and specialized microfinance institutions.
 
 

 Challenges
 Major challenges include high **operational costs**, dependency on donor funding, and ensuring **social impact**.
